hypotheses.H_a0: (exploratory, seen data) The v0.6.0 event is late because it is a window MEAN: from a calm window a single maximally surprising observation cannot cross tau/2 (Exact arithmetic above), so the first event after a drift comes at the earliest with the second surprising observation, and the certificate issued in between is stale. Inferred; tested only descriptively on the sealed study-008 drift4 traces (diagnostic, not gated).
hypotheses.H_a: There exists a certification rule with SYNCHRONOUS events (an event at the very step whose observation is surprising or falsifies a certificate) that, on held-out 2x2 data, has 0 non-drift false certificates on drift4, total drift4 false certificates <= 0.5 x v0.90 control, AND pooled in-family coverage no worse than A2 by more than 0.03 (CI lower >= -0.05), while keeping G1 and G2 at 0. Two candidate rules (S7, SC7) are tested; H_a is supported only if ONE arm passes all four gates.

event_triggers.E1: v0.6.0 event, unchanged: after observing step u, residual (mean of the last W=8 surprises, 12 d.p.) > tau x 0.5, or a window-tier event (as brute/driftsound._note_event)
event_triggers.E2: falsified certificate: the forecast for the taken action at step u carried a conditional certificate c and the observation at u is incompatible with c (bit c not in the observation mask). Constant-free.
event_triggers.E3: single-step surprise: s_u = -ln compatible_mass(published probabilities for u, observation u) > tau (tau6 for 2x2, tau7 for breadth; the frozen ALARM threshold applied to one step instead of the window mean). No new constant. Exact: tau6 = 1.645215 > ln 4 = 1.386294 and tau7 = 2.07944154168 > ln 8 = 2.07944154167984 (margin ~2e-13), so a forecast spread uniformly over all codes never triggers E3; E3 needs the realised observation to have had probability < e^-tau (0.1930 for 2x2, 0.1250 for 8 codes).
event_triggers.note: Inferred: when the published forecast is a certified one, E2 implies E3 (the falsified code carried >= 1-3eps/4 mass, so the compatible mass is <= 3 x eps/4 = 0.015, s >= 4.2 > tau6); E2 is kept as an explicit, constant-free trigger and each event records which triggers fired. Alarms (F4 RESIDUAL_SURPRISE), resume, probabilities and LU-R are NOT changed by E2/E3.

arms.S7: brute.syncevent.SyncEventLearner(rule="RO"), subclass of the frozen v0.6.0 DriftSoundLearner(rule="RO") (R6). Identical to R6 except that the event set is E1 OR E2 OR E3 (synchronous events). Recency-opened edges as R6: if the latest event s* satisfies t - s* < W, Y1k-recent with t0 = max(0, s*-1). Targets G3-prime.
arms.SC7: brute.syncevent.SyncEventLearner(rule="CTR"), subclass of DriftSoundLearner(rule="CT") (C6). Certify code c if the A5 Y1k check certifies c, OR all of: (i) the tracked-state projection of the full-history region (A2 rule) is the single code c, (ii) no event (E1, E2 or E3) at any step u with t - u < W (RECENCY-EXPIRING calm, replacing C6's whole-session calm), (iii) t >= burn_in. While an event is recent (t - s* < W) the R6/S7 Y1k-recent path is used instead of Y1k. Targets GA1 (coverage and drift together).

planning_rule.applicable: at a step where the A5 LU-R score is computed (family and margin supported, no active alarm) and t >= burn_in; at every other step P7 takes exactly the action A5's policy would take from the same learner state
planning_rule.counts: n_{a,c} = number of (machine, fibre state) pairs of the current RegionK region (<= 4 states, canonical first-visit machines) predicting code c under action a: the per-code fibre counts DEFINED by the frozen brute/modelcount.py (sha256 6f46232a82ceb2998ba291653ed18e440164d408a385144259aa0a5e3aa6efb4), called unchanged; N_a = sum_c n_{a,c}
planning_rule.source_order: (1) explicit enumeration of the region's canonical machines with blocking clauses, used if it completes with <= 10^4 machines within 3 s (pairs then computed in plain Python by replaying the evidence); else (2) pyganak==2.8.0 projected counts (8 counts, 2 x 4 codes) with the per-count budget
planning_rule.objective_1step: E1(a) = sum_c n_{a,c}^2 / N_a (expected surviving pairs after observing the code of a, uniform weight on pairs, masking ignored: declared approximation)
planning_rule.objective_2step: only when source (1) completed: E2(a) = sum_c (n_{a,c}/N_a) x min_b E1(b | a, c), computed exactly by simulation on the explicit pair list; the action is argmin E2, ties broken by E1, then by the A5 LU-R choice
planning_rule.choice: argmin_a of E2 if available, else E1; exact rational comparison; ties -> A5 LU-R choice
planning_rule.fallback: any UNKNOWN count (timeout/error/counter unavailable) or exhausted budget -> the decision takes the A5 LU-R choice and is recorded as fallback with reason; never imputed
planning_rule.isolation: counts influence ONLY the action choice. Certification, status, reason, probabilities, surprise, alarm and resume of P7 are computed by the frozen A5 code from P7's own (action, observation) history; brute/planner.py may not import or monkeypatch anything that A5's predict/observe call

budget.per_decision: 15 s wall for all counting of one decision
budget.per_case: 150 s of counting per case; later decisions of that case fall back
budget.block: planning block wall clock <= 60 min (6 workers); at the cap, unfinished cases are killed and scored as missing (GP1 FAIL via the completeness clause)

planning_rule.label: the objective is a heuristic (Inferred); the counts it consumes are Exact where pyganak's documented guarantee is exact and the enumeration completed

default_policy_rule: No auto-promotion: the release default stays the v0.5.0 rule (Y1k, LU-R) regardless of outcome. A rule passing GA1 or GP1 becomes a candidate default only after an owner decision AND a fresh held-out replication in a later study.

xcheck_backend.file: brute/xcheck_sat_incremental.py (adopted, byte-identical) driven by the new experiments/v070_xcheck.py (no import of brute/region.py, brute/geometry.py or any enumeration code)
xcheck_backend.encoding: the brute/xcheck_sat (v0.6.0) encoding solved incrementally: one live CaDiCaL instance per (case, bound N), evidence added layer by layer under activation literals, symmetry=True (first-visit state naming S_0[0] and S_t[q] -> V_{t-1}[q-1])
xcheck_backend.solver: CaDiCaL 1.9.5 via python-sat (cadical195); RegionK uses Glucose3
xcheck_backend.per_query: support, saturation, Y1k and Y1k-recent queries as in GX2-prime: uniqueness by UNSAT, abstention by two SAT models each decoded and REPLAYED in plain Python against the evidence; BS7/BSC7 events (E1/E2/E3) and SC7 recency calm are recomputed by v070_xcheck.py from the re-derived support sets and recomputed probabilities
xcheck_backend.budget: 2,000,000 conflicts per solve call; a query over budget makes the step UNCHECKED (counted, never a mismatch, never a pass)
xcheck_backend.independence_caveat: NOT an independent encoding in the strong sense (labelled "second encoding by the same author"): (1) same author as RegionK and the learners; (2) symmetry=True uses first-visit canonical state naming, the SAME symmetry-reduction idea RegionK uses, so a shared conceptual error in that reduction could be invisible to both; the incremental harness argues (Inferred) that every query is invariant under state renaming, it does not prove it mechanically; (3) it differs from RegionK in solver (CaDiCaL vs Glucose3), variable layout (direct T[q][a][r], E[q][c], path S[t][q]), incremental layering and Python witness replay; (4) the post-release run on study-008 (0 mismatches) is development knowledge on seen data, not v0.7.0 evidence. The no-symmetry spot check exists to keep one encoding without the shared assumption.
xcheck_backend.spot_check: the same harness with symmetry=False on the 24 xcheck_spot_sample cases (B5): 2,000,000 conflicts per query, 2 workers, 30 min wall cap; steps of a case unfinished at the cap are UNCHECKED

modelcount.use: P7 action choice only (planning_rule); counts are never used by certification, alarm, resume or any other arm
